items.title: A complete devissage persists under an affine base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that after an arbitrary affine base change S' -> S every member of a complete devissage family (Z_k, Y_k, i_k, pi_k, G_k, alpha_k)_{k=1..n} has a primed counterpart that is again a complete devissage of the pulled-back pair F'/X'/S' (statement lines 1272-1284). The reduction to the one step case is immediate, but the two remaining conditions have to be checked through the pushforward: the cokernel of alpha_k must commute with base change, which is not formal because Coker is formed after the finite morphism pi_k, and condition (2) must be preserved through the residue-field extension kappa(xi_k) -> kappa(xi'_k) at the generic points of the fibres (proof lines 1295-1309). Both steps are short and consist of identifying a fibre of a pullback with a scalar extension, which is why the claim is H2.
